title: t4 (null-weight-shuffled): no behaviour to explain
label: null result: no mechanism claimed
behavior: BOS + 6 tokens from 5 symbols; the model is supposed to output one symbol at the last position, matching the answers recorded in the bench dataset.
summary: The loaded checkpoint does not perform the behaviour. Against the dataset's recorded answers it scores 21.0% on 200 inputs (E0003) and 21.8% on 500 fresh inputs (E0004); chance for 5 symbols is 20%. The correct-vs-incorrect logit difference averages about zero with a spread of ~53 and is the same on clean and corrupt inputs. Following the protocol, the investigation stopped after the baseline: no function, no circuit, no predict() and no verification are claimed. All numbers are from local-full (full precision). 4 of 25 experiments used.

claims.text: The loaded model agrees with the dataset's recorded answers only at chance: 0.21 on n=200 (seed 1), where the pre-registered prediction of >=0.98 was refuted.
The chance-level result replicates on an independent larger sample: 0.218 on n=500 (seed 2), pre-registered as <=0.30 and confirmed.
The logit difference between recorded-correct and incorrect answers carries no signal: mean 2.06 (std 54.1) on clean vs 0.05 on corrupt in E0003, and -4.23 (std 52.9) vs -4.52 in E0004.
No attention head or MLP layer is claimed as part of a circuit, because there is no behaviour for a circuit to implement.

limitations: The task statement says the dataset answers are the model's own outputs; measured agreement is at chance, so either the checkpoint that was loaded is not the one that produced the labels or its weights have been altered. This investigation cannot tell which.
The investigation stopped at the baseline; nothing was measured about what the loaded model computes instead (it is deterministic, so it computes some function, but not the labelled one).
The only screen (E0002, attribution patching, exploratory) gave estimates 10-30x larger than the clean-corrupt gap and was not used for any claim.
verify_hypothesis was not run: there is no hypothesis to verify.
open_questions: Do the recorded labels follow a simple rule? In the 64 examples of E0001 they fit 'the last token selects one of positions 1-3, then a table lookup on (last token, selected token)'. This was fitted by eye, is untested on held-out data, and is a property of the labels, not of this model.
What function does the loaded checkpoint itself compute, if one cares about it independently of the benchmark labels?
overall_status: unverified (no verification run) · null result: no mechanism claimed

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The model produces its own recorded outputs deterministically on the bench dataset (the behaviour exists and is far from the 20% chance level).

prediction.statement: Clean accuracy against the recorded answers is at least 98%
